claims.claim: Vylor became an independent, publicly traded company when Corteva spun off its Seed Business on October 1 2026 through a tax‑free in‑kind dividend to Corteva shareholders.
claims.quote: On October 1, 2026, Corteva, Inc. (“Corteva” or “the company”) completed its previously announced separation into two independent, publicly traded companies – … the other comprising its Seed Business (“Vylor”, “our,” “we,” or “the Seed Business”) – through a pro rata dividend in‑kind of all of the then‑issued and outstanding shares of common stock of Vylor to holders of Corteva’s common stock as of the close of business on September 24, 2026 (the “Vylor Separation”).

claims.claim: The Seed Business develops and sells commercial seed that combines advanced germplasm and trait technologies to maximize farmer yield potential.
claims.quote: The Seed Business is a global leader in developing and supplying commercial seed combining advanced germplasm and traits that offer maximum yield potential for farmers around the world.

claims.claim: The company is a leader in many key seed markets, including North America corn and soybeans, Europe corn and sunflower, and Brazil, India, South Africa and Argentina corn.
claims.quote: The Company is a leader in many key seed markets, including North America corn and soybeans, Europe corn and sunflower, as well as Brazil, India, South Africa and Argentina corn.

claims.claim: Management reports that pro‑forma net sales for the nine‑month YTD period increased 4% versus the prior year, with organic sales up 2% driven by North America.
claims.quote: Pro forma net sales1 increased 4% versus prior year. Pro forma organic2 sales increased 2% in the same period, led by North America.

claims.claim: Price/mix was up 3% in the Americas and 5% in Rest of World, reflecting continued execution of the price‑for‑value strategy and higher licensing income.
claims.quote: Price/mix was up 3% with continued execution on the Company’s price for value strategy and increased licensing income.

claims.claim: Management plans to grow the Seed Business through gene‑editing, biofuels, hybrid wheat, expanded crop offerings, and M&A.
claims.quote: The Seed Business plans to grow through opportunities in gene editing, biofuels, hybrid wheat, expanded crop offerings, and mergers and acquisitions.

claims.claim: The Board authorized a new $3 billion multi‑year share repurchase program, providing flexibility for capital return to shareholders.
claims.quote: The Board also authorized a new $3 billion multi-year share repurchase program.

claims.claim: Vylor’s Investor Day highlighted a pipeline of 12 technology platforms, including seven new corn platforms beginning in 2028 and a gene‑edited multi‑disease‑resistant corn platform.
claims.quote: Corn Seven new corn technology platforms will be launched over the next decade – starting in 2028 – including the industry's first‑ever trait designed to improve yield and yield stability.

claims.claim: A $0.13 per share dividend was declared for 2026, indicating a commitment to returning cash to shareholders.
claims.quote: On October 22, 2026, the Company announced that its Board of Directors authorized a common stock dividend of $0.13 per share, payable December 7, 2026.

claims.claim: The company remains subject to ongoing litigation and environmental liabilities that could materially affect results.
claims.quote: The Seed Business is subject to various legal proceedings … it is not possible to predict the outcome of these various proceedings, as considerable uncertainty exists.

claims.claim: Risk factors include potential additional costs from the Vylor Separation, such as unexpected expenses or litigation.
claims.quote: risks related to the Vylor Separation including, but not limited to, whether the objectives of the separation will be achieved; the terms, structure, benefits and costs of any action or transaction resulting from the separation; unexpected costs or expenses resulting from the separation, and the risk of any litigation as a result of, or relating to, the separation.

claims.claim: Judgment: Prioritize accelerating the licensing business (Vylor One) to capture the $500 million gross licensing income target for 2027, leveraging the demonstrated increase in licensing revenue noted in the YTD results.
claims.quote: In addition, via Vylor One, its new licensing business, the Company expects to deliver approximately $500 million in gross licensing income in 2027.

gaps: The 10‑Q does not provide a standalone GAAP earnings or cash‑flow forecast for the Seed Business post‑separation, so any forward‑looking financial guidance for Vylor alone cannot be cited.
Detailed R&D expenditure figures for the Seed Business are not disclosed in the interim filing; therefore the magnitude of investment required for the gene‑editing pipeline cannot be quantified.
insight: Insight: The Board authorized a $3 billion multi‑year share repurchase program — 10‑Q line 2151: "The Board also authorized a new $3 billion multi-year share repurchase program."
